concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: The Indian textile industry was subjected to discriminatory trade practices. Which of the following policies harmed the Indian textile industry under British rule?

options.text: Equal tariffs on imports and exports
Imposition of heavy duties on Indian exports to Britain

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Imposition of heavy duties on Indian exports to Britain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **British colonial policies** imposed **heavy duties and tariffs** on Indian textile exports to Britain, making Indian goods less competitive in the British market.
 
• These discriminatory trade practices were designed to promote the **British textile industry** at the expense of the Indian textile industry.
 
• The imposition of high tariffs led to a significant decline in Indian textile exports, which were once renowned globally for their **quality, craftsmanship, and uniqueness**.
 
• Indian weavers and artisans faced severe hardships due to reduced demand for their goods, resulting in widespread **unemployment and economic distress**.
 
• The policy also forced Indian consumers to buy British-manufactured goods, which were imported into India without significant tariffs, further benefiting the British economy.
 
• This exploitation contributed to the **deindustrialization** of India during the colonial period, as traditional industries like textiles were deliberately undermined.
 
• The adverse impact of these policies on India's economy highlighted the exploitative nature of British colonial rule and the need for economic independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equal tariffs on imports and exports**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because the British did not impose equal tariffs. They deliberately imposed **unequal and discriminatory tariffs** to favor their own industries.
 
 
 
• **Free trade within India**__
 __
 
• While free trade within India might sound beneficial, under British rule, this concept was manipulated to serve British economic interests rather than support Indian industries.
 
• Indian manufacturers faced competition from **cheap British imports**, which were often dumped in the Indian market.
 
 
 
• **Export subsidies**__
 
 
• The British did not provide export subsidies for Indian textiles. Instead, they imposed **restrictions and high duties** to suppress Indian exports and promote British products.
